children: The order comes as Trai reviews its Quality of Service framework, and telecom operators face continued scrutiny over network performance

Vodafone Idea (Vi) has been imposed a financial disincentive of Rs 2 lakh by the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (Trai) for failing to comply with prescribed Quality of Service (QoS) standards in various areas during October 2025. The telecom operator received the order on 14 September 2026 and disclosed the development in a stock exchange filing on 15 September.

The order relates to non-compliance with the Standards of Quality of Service of Access (Wireline and Wireless) and Broadband (Wireline and Wireless) Service Regulations, 2024. Vi said the maximum financial impact from the order is limited to the disincentive levied by TRAI.
Vi said it is reviewing the order and evaluating the next steps in the matter. The company did not disclose any additional operational or financial impact arising from the regulatory action.

The filing was made pursuant to Regulation 30 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) Listing Regulations. The company has not provided details of the specific QoS parameters or service areas that resulted in the latest disincentive.

Trai’s QoS framework requires telecom service providers to meet prescribed service benchmarks. Where operators fail to meet the stipulated benchmarks, the regulator seeks an explanation from the service provider before deciding on any financial disincentive.

The latest order comes amid broader regulatory scrutiny of service quality across India’s telecom sector. Parliament was informed in August that telecom operators had faced a combined Rs 1.9 crore in penalties for QoS violations during FY26, with BSNL accounting for the highest amount at Rs 57.5 lakh, followed by Bharti Airtel at Rs 48 lakh, MTNL at Rs 37 lakh, Vodafone Idea at Rs 31 lakh and Reliance Jio at Rs 17 lakh.

The Rs 2 lakh disincentive disclosed by Vi on September 15 is a separate regulatory order and should not be treated as part of the Rs 31 lakh figure reported for FY26. The earlier figure represents penalties imposed on the company during the financial year, while the latest disclosure relates specifically to the October 2025 QoS non-compliance matter.

Trai is also examining changes to its QoS framework. In August 2026, the regulator issued a consultation paper on proposed amendments to the 2024 Standards of Quality of Service of Access and Broadband Services Regulations, with Vodafone Idea among the telecom operators that submitted comments.

The proposed review covers the existing QoS framework for wireless and wireline access and broadband services. The development comes as operators face closer scrutiny over network performance and compliance with prescribed service standards.

For Vi, the latest Rs 2 lakh order has limited financial significance based on the company’s filing. However, the disclosure comes against a wider regulatory focus on telecom service quality and the enforcement of QoS requirements across operators.
